issues.description: The solution defines the pixel-setting routine with the label '.set_pixel' (leading dot) while the template (and main) expect a symbol named 'set_pixel'. A label starting with a dot is a different symbol/visibility in many assemblers (and may be local), so the 'call set_pixel' in main will not resolve to '.set_pixel'. This is a structural/visibility mismatch between template and solution that will prevent the program from assembling or running as intended and will confuse students about the correct routine name to implement/call.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the routine name consistent. Rename the solution's '.set_pixel:' label to 'set_pixel:' (remove the leading dot), or update the call sites to call '.set_pixel' and ensure the label has appropriate linkage (declare global if needed). This preserves the intended interface (call set_pixel with x in EAX, y in EBX, color in ECX) and avoids assembly/link failures.

issues.description: The problem statement and the template refer to the subroutine by the name 'set_pixel', but the solution defines the routine as '.set_pixel' (leading dot). This creates a naming mismatch across artifacts: students reading the solution to understand how to implement the required 'set_pixel' routine may not immediately recognize '.set_pixel' as the same entity (and in some assemblers a leading dot may denote a different scope). This inconsistency increases mapping effort and may confuse students trying to match the problem requirement to the solution code.
issues.suggested_fix: Use the same subroutine name across all artifacts. Rename the solution's label from '.set_pixel' to 'set_pixel' (or alternatively change the template/problem to reference '.set_pixel' consistently). Preferably align to 'set_pixel' to match the problem statement and template and avoid assembler-specific scoping conventions.
